llm.summary: The skill is mostly what it says (it uses PyAutoGUI to automate typing into WeChat), but there is a functional mismatch: the README implies it can 'send files' while the script only types the file path as chat text, and automation of keyboard/mouse carries inherent risk of accidentally sending sensitive content.

dimensions.detail: Name/description align with the code: the script automates keyboard shortcuts and typing to interact with WeChat using PyAutoGUI. However, SKILL.md and examples imply true file sending/attachment, while the script's send_file implementation merely writes the file path text into the chat and presses Enter (does not attach/upload the file). This is a user-facing functionality mismatch that could mislead users.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent/user to run the provided script and to install pyautogui. The runtime instructions and script restrict themselves to keyboard/mouse automation and local file existence checks only (no network calls, no hidden endpoints). Concerns: (1) the skill will type arbitrary text into whatever window is focused — if content comes from an upstream agent or user-supplied data this could leak sensitive information; (2) the 'send file' behavior does not actually attach files, which may cause surprising results; (3) the SKILL.md example embeds a specific local path (D:\clawSpaces) which assumes a Windows environment and may mislead users on other platforms.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec; dependency is a standard pip package (pyautogui) listed in SKILL.md. This is a low-risk installation pattern (no arbitrary downloads, no archive extraction).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no environment variables, no credentials, and no config paths. The code does not access environment variables or external credentials. The requested access is proportionate to the stated purpose.

llm.guidance:
This script automates typing and keyboard shortcuts in WeChat — review and test it carefully before use. Important points:
- The script does not actually attach files: --file will make the script type the file path into chat, not upload the file. Use --no-send to preview what it will type.
- Because it simulates keyboard/mouse, do not move the mouse or type while it runs; enable pyautogui.FAILSAFE (already set) so you can abort by moving the mouse to a corner.
- Confirm the Ctrl+Alt+W and Ctrl+F shortcuts match your WeChat setup; otherwise the automation may target the wrong window.
- Avoid passing sensitive secrets as messages to be typed automatically; an agent or script could accidentally send them.
- If you install pyautogui, get it from the official PyPI package (pip install pyautogui) and inspect the script locally before running.
- If you need true file attachment behavior, modify the script to interact with WeChat's attachment UI (current behavior may be surprising to users expecting a real file upload).
